name: stat
description: Displays detailed status of files or filesystems: size, blocks, inode, permissions, ownership, and all timestamps.

flags.description: -printf FORMAT: control the output with a format string (%s size, %y human time, %a access rights, %U user, %G group, %i inode).
Report filesystem status instead of file status.
Use a more verbose, labeled output format.

examples.output:
File: notes.txt
  Size: 220         Blocks: 8          IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 8,2   Inode: 131073   Links: 1
Access: (0644/-rw-r--r--)  Uid: ( 1000/  user)   Gid: ( 1000/  user)
Modify: 2025-01-10 09:15:03.000000000 +0100
examples.explanation: Shows the inode number, permission bits with octal value, owner, and the timestamps (Access, Modify, Change).
Custom format: prints each filename and its size in bytes.
Quick permission check: octal mode, owner, group, and path in one line.

about: stat reports the raw inode metadata. The three timestamps are: atime (last read), mtime (last content modification), and ctime (last inode change — including permission or ownership changes, not just content). There is no "creation time" in classic Linux inodes; some filesystems expose a birth time (statx) but support varies.
useCases: Inspect exact permissions and ownership in octal form.
Check inode numbers when troubleshooting hard links.
mistakes: Confusing ctime with creation time — ctime means "change time" of the inode.
